newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Kiwi holds day's gains, TWI firms, in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: Kiwi holds day's gains, TWI firms, in thin trade.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar closed a shade firmer, above the 68 cent figure against the U.S. unit, after steady but thin trade on Tuesday that dealers said reflected some apprehension over Australian and domestic rates.
The TWI ended stronger, supported by dollar/yen firmness.

"People were maybe expecting another fall in the Aussie on the back of a possible rate cut, but that never happened. The market still looks fairly short of Aussie, so we'll just have to wait and see what comes out later in the week," one dealer said.
While some Australian market observers expect a signal for a new rate cut tomorrow, New Zealand has its own monetary event.

Reserve Bank Governor Don Brash is due before Parliament's Finance and Expenditure Select Committee (FEC) at 9.00 a.m. (2100 GMT) for a routine debriefing following his Monetary Policy Statement last Friday.

Some debt and currency market dealers say Brash's answers to questions about subsequent market movements, especially after a weaker-than-expected GDP figure on Monday, might provide new insight into the bank's view on the degree of monetary easing that current market conditions have put in place.
Nevertheless, his comments are not seen shifting the kiwi very far from its recent 67-1/2 to 68-1/2 U.S. cent range.
